concepts.title: Numbers Can Tell Us Things
concepts.definition: Numbers can describe situations cleverly: patterns of numbers can stand for children standing in order of height or other hidden facts, and reading the pattern reveals the story behind the numbers.
concepts.key_idea: A number pattern is a coded story: decoding the rule tells the hidden situation.

concepts.title: Supercells
concepts.definition: In a row or grid of numbers, a cell is a supercell when its number is bigger than its neighbours beside it; marking supercells turns number grids into games of observation.
concepts.key_idea: A supercell is a local champion: bigger than its immediate neighbours, even if not the biggest overall.

concepts.title: Kaprekar's Routine to 6174
concepts.definition: Take a four-digit number, arrange its digits from biggest to smallest and from smallest to biggest, and subtract: repeating this Kaprekar routine lands every four-digit number (with not all digits equal) on the constant 6174.
concepts.key_idea: One subtraction step shuffles numbers towards a fixed point: 6174 keeps returning to itself.

concepts.title: Patterns of Numbers on the Number Line
concepts.section: 3.3 Patterns of numbers on the number line
concepts.definition: Marking numbers on the number line reveals families: numbers with the same digit sum cluster in colour-classes, multiples of a number sit at even gaps, and games like saying a word for multiples of 3 make the structure audible.
concepts.key_idea: The number line is a home for patterns: gaps, jumps and colour-classes make number families visible.
